# GIMP feature inventory (parity reference for Gesso)

> **Provenance note (2026-09-26):** verbatim copy of the GIMP 3.2.6 inventory compiled for the Gesso parity plan, rows `GP-0001` to `GP-4891`, under its original title: GIMP 3 feature inventory for Gesso parity. The ids are stable and each is placed in exactly one row of [`../gesso-parity.md`](../gesso-parity.md). Do not renumber; a future GIMP version appends new ids after GP-4891 (see [`../README.md`](../README.md)).

> **Access:** no limits applied. The GIMP 3.2 user manual (all 760 English pages) was mirrored and parsed in full, together with the GEGL operations reference and the GIMP 3.0 to 3.2.6 release notes; rows are therefore very granular (one row per documented option), which the catalog folds into features.

- Product: GIMP (GNU Image Manipulation Program), 3.x series
- Latest stable version inventoried: GIMP 3.2.6, released 2026-09-10 (https://www.gimp.org/news/2026/09/10/gimp-3-2-6-released/)
- 3.2.0 released 2026-03-14 (https://www.gimp.org/news/2026/03/14/gimp-3-2-released/); 3.2.2 on 2026-03-28; 3.2.4 on 2026-04-19; 3.0.0 released 2025-03-16 (https://www.gimp.org/news/2025/03/16/gimp-3-0-released/)
- Inventory date: 2026-09-26
- Total rows: 4891

- GIMP 3.0 release notes: https://www.gimp.org/release-notes/gimp-3.0.html
- GIMP 3.2 release notes: https://www.gimp.org/release-notes/gimp-3.2.html
- GIMP 3.2.2 news: https://www.gimp.org/news/2026/03/28/gimp-3-2-2-released/
- GIMP 3.2.4 news: https://www.gimp.org/news/2026/04/19/gimp-3-2-4-released/
- GIMP 3.2.6 news: https://www.gimp.org/news/2026/09/10/gimp-3-2-6-released/

- Third-party plug-in projects (AI and automation rows only): https://github.com/intel/openvino-ai-plugins-gimp , https://github.com/kritiksoman/GIMP-ML , https://github.com/bootchk/resynthesizer , https://gmic.eu/

## Method notes

- The GIMP 3.2 manual (docs.gimp.org/3.2/en, which is the manual for the current 3.2.x line) was crawled in full (760 pages) and parsed with a script. Every tool, menu command, filter, dialog, preference page, and export dialog page yields one feature row. Every documented option term (DocBook variablelist dt entry) on those pages yields its own row, and combined terms such as "Add Alpha Channel, Remove Alpha Channel" are split into one row per term. Nested options are written as Parent > Child in the Feature column.
- Where = the menu path taken from the page Activating section (a handful corrected by hand), or Tool Options > Tool for tool options, Canvas > Tool for key-modifier and on-canvas behaviors, Edit > Preferences > Page for preferences, and File > Export As... > Format for export options.
- What it does = first sentence of the manual text for that item. When the manual only says "see the common options", the text of the matching common option (Selection, Paint, or Transform tools common options, or the common filter options) is substituted and prefixed "Common option:".
- Rows for GIMP 3.0 to 3.2.6 changes that the manual does not describe as their own page (link layers, vector layers, Overwrite mode, Vibrance, new formats, 3.2.x fixes with user-visible behavior) come from gimp.org release notes and news posts and are gathered in the Release highlights area and the format matrix.
- GEGL operations: every operation listed at gegl.org/operations is included except pure I/O, buffer, cache, meta, and basic geometry plumbing ops. These are reachable in GIMP through Tools > GEGL Operation and the Help > GEGL Filter Browser even when no menu entry exists; many duplicate a menu filter and are listed so Gesso can map op ids.
- Category column: core by default; format for file format rows; print for Print, Print Size, PostScript/EPS and soft-proofing; video for Filters > Animation, animation playback and optimization, and animation-related export options (GIF, APNG, FLI, MNG, ANI); automation for Script-Fu, Python-Fu, consoles, Procedure/Plug-in/GEGL Filter browsers, GEGL Graph, and plug-in APIs; ai for machine learning features. GIMP 3.2.6 has no built-in AI; third-party AI plug-ins are listed and marked ai.
- Kinds used: tool, tool-option, command, dialog, dialog-option, filter, filter-option, blend-mode, format, format-option, preference, behavior. Context-menu and dialog button entries are command. Key modifiers and on-canvas handling are behavior. Porter-Duff and SVG compositing GEGL ops are blend-mode.
- Rows were de-duplicated on Feature + Where + Kind. The same option can legitimately appear under several tools or filters; each occurrence is kept because Gesso must implement it per tool.
- Text normalization: arrows written as >, no pipes, no em or en dashes, degree sign written as deg. Every table row was validated to have exactly 7 columns.
- Access gaps: none blocking. All manual pages downloaded directly. The manual has no pages yet for a few 3.2 additions (Vibrance, link and vector layer dialogs, Overwrite mode, Paint Select, Seamless Clone and N-Point Deformation tool options); those rows use release notes or the Preferences Playground page, so their option-level detail is thinner than for documented tools. Import-only format options (beyond PDF and PostScript import) are not documented in the manual and are covered at format level only.

| GP-3512 | Color-dodge (svg:color-dodge) | blend-mode | Tools > GEGL Operation > svg:color-dodge | SVG blend operation color-dodge (<code>if cA * aB + cB * aA >= aA * aB: d = aA * aB + cA * (1 - aB) + cB * (1 - aA) otherwise: d = (cA == aA ? 1 : cB * aA / (aA == 0 ? 1 : 1 - cA / aA)) + cA * (1 - aB) + cB * (1 - aA)</code>). | core | https://gegl.org/operations/svg-color-dodge.html |
| GP-3513 | svg:darken (svg:darken) | blend-mode | Tools > GEGL Operation > svg:darken | SVG blend operation darken (<code>d = MIN (cA * aB, cB * aA) + cA * (1 - aB) + cB * (1 - aA)</code>). | core | https://gegl.org/operations/svg-darken.html |
| GP-3514 | svg:difference (svg:difference) | blend-mode | Tools > GEGL Operation > svg:difference | SVG blend operation difference (<code>d = cA + cB - 2 * (MIN (cA * aB, cB * aA))</code>). | core | https://gegl.org/operations/svg-difference.html |

| GP-3517 | Dst-in (svg:dst-in) | blend-mode | Tools > GEGL Operation > svg:dst-in | Porter Duff operation dst-in (d = cB * aA). | core | https://gegl.org/operations/svg-dst-in.html |

| GP-3521 | Hard-light (svg:hard-light) | blend-mode | Tools > GEGL Operation > svg:hard-light | SVG blend operation hard-light (<code>if 2 * cA < aA: d = 2 * cA * cB + cA * (1 - aB) + cB * (1 - aA) otherwise: d = aA * aB - 2 * (aB - cB) * (aA - cA) + cA * (1 - aB) + cB * (1 - aA)</code>). | core | https://gegl.org/operations/svg-hard-light.html |
